derivation: Written by applying contract/semantics.md to the recorded frames by hand.
NOT generated by running any binding — expectations produced by the code
under test would only prove that code agrees with itself.
bucket_start, step by step, for the single bar in this fixture:
1. ts_str '2026-04/18-13:30:45' read as America/New_York. 2026-04-18 is
inside EDT (UTC-4), giving 2026-04-18T17:30:45Z.
2. §2.1 floor to the minute            -> 17:30:00Z
3. §2 right label -> left label, minus one tf (1m) -> 17:29:00Z
4. §2.2 snap to the 1m UTC grid        -> 17:29:00Z (already on it)
So the bar covers [17:29, 17:30), which is 13:29 ET.
Note step 2 is load-bearing here and nowhere else in this fixture: the
harness reuses a tick's :45 timestamp for the bar, which real EasyLanguage
never does. That is deliberate — see notes.
There is no ts_utc field to cross-check against any more; this protocol
carries the raw string and the receive clock only. The derivation above
used the IANA tzdb through Python's zoneinfo, independently of both the
DLL and the binding.
Two things are per-run and were read from this recording rather than
derived: `sid`, and each tick's `timestamp`. §1 makes the DLL's
receive-side `ts` authoritative for a tick, so the expectation is that
epoch rendered as UTC — a mechanical conversion, not a parse. A bar's
bucket_start comes from ts_str, which the harness hard-codes.
notes: VXX is an index/breadth symbol per semantics.md §3.2, so its bid/ask MUST
be null even though the wire carries 449.99/450.01 exactly like every
other frame. This is the rule a new binding is most likely to miss, and
the reason this fixture exists.
seq is per-symbol and shared between kinds (semantics.md §6.1): SPY runs
1, 2, 3 with the bar taking 3. All six frames carry one sid.
The harness reuses the tick timestamp (13:30:45) for the bar, so this
fixture exercises semantics.md §2.1: bucket_start is floored to the
minute, giving 17:30:00Z rather than 17:30:45Z, before the left-label
step lands it on 17:29:00Z. Real EL supplies an already aligned time,
which makes the flooring a no-op and easy to leave unwritten — it was,
until this fixture caught it.
The five el_* quantities are EasyLanguage's reserved words verbatim, and
a binding must store them the same way: no selection, no conversion. The
harness picks internally consistent intraday values — el_volume equals
el_upticks, and el_ticks equals el_upticks + el_downticks — which is the
relationship real intraday data has and which a binding must not 'fix'.
Bars carry no bid/ask at all in this protocol. There is nothing for a
binding to decide about a bar quote any more.
sid is the publisher session id in epoch MICROseconds (semantics.md
§6.3). Compare it for equality only; it is not a timestamp field.
Only wire-derivable fields are asserted. Anything a binding computes on
top (session tagging, retention) is outside the contract.
